title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements, credit controls and maker settings are supported by Microsoft's documentation. Targeted searches found no documented switch dedicated to the agent node or automation for its human-assistance setting.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent for reasoning.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Attached tools let the agent perform actions.
claims.quote: Tools give the agent the ability to do actions such as send a message, query a record, run a search, or call an API.

claims.claim: The agent can read attached knowledge sources before returning a result.
claims.quote: Knowledge gives the agent something to read. When you ask the agent a question, it can ground its answer in the sources you attach instead of relying only on what the model already knows.

claims.claim: The agent response becomes dynamic content for subsequent workflow steps.
claims.quote: The agent response then becomes available as dynamic content that you can use in any subsequent step.

claims.claim: An existing agent is selected from a list of published agents.
claims.quote: An existing agent: Select a published agent from a list.

claims.claim: An existing agent runs with its already-configured instructions, tools and knowledge.
claims.quote: The agent runs with whatever instructions, tools, and knowledge it was already configured with.

claims.claim: New agent for this workflow configures an inline agent's instructions, tools, knowledge and output shape inside the node, travelling with the workflow.
claims.quote: New agent for this workflow: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow. The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote: Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow? No. An inline agent is scoped to its workflow.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No agent-node-specific credit rate is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "rate" "credits". Read agent-node-workflow, agents-experience/billing-credit-overview and manage-usage-github-copilot-harness; search also returned requirements-messages-management, explicitly scoped to the standard harness. No node-specific rate found.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Credits are charged to the environment where the work runs, rather than individual makers.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan, and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.claim: Consumption uses prepaid capacity or the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan

claims.claim: Capacity management requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role managing licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Environment credit allocation is under Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Licensing. ... Under Products, select Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Allocating credits and clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant contains prepaid consumption at environment level.
claims.quote: To contain prepaid consumption, allocate a defined amount of Copilot Credits to the environment and turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.claim: Disabling tenant-pool draw does not stop consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go billing plan.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.claim: Azure budgets send notifications without stopping Copilot Studio consumption.
claims.quote: Azure budgets and alerts send notifications but don't stop Copilot Studio consumption.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads, not only agent nodes.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: Changing shared capacity can affect other agents, workflows and features in the same environment.
claims.quote: Changes to shared capacity can affect other Copilot Studio agents, workflows, and features in the same environment.

claims.claim: Eligible Copilot Studio environments with no allocation configuration default to drawing from tenant capacity.
claims.quote: For eligible Copilot Studio environments, Draw from the available capacity in my tenant is selected by default when no allocation configuration exists.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule makes the tenant-draw setting read-only at environment level.
claims.quote: When you publish a rule, it governs every environment in the group. The environment-level setting becomes read-only in the Power Platform admin center, and programmatic requests can't override it.

claims.claim: Programmatic updates cannot override a published environment-group tenant-draw rule.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and allocation body
claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 with the supplied scope and allocatedEntitlements body sets MCSMessages allocation and disables TenantPool draw.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put ... -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion" ... scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId } ... entitlementId = "MCSMessages" ... allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 } ... @{ ruleType = "TenantPool"; enabled = $false }

claims.claim: The allocation request requires authenticated authorisation and application/json content.
claims.quote: $headers = @{ Authorization = "Bearer $($auth.AccessToken)" } ... -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body $allocationBody

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: The node page does not document the identity used by attached connector actions or SharePoint knowledge.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Data policies govern Power Platform connector tools in Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from using Power Platform connectors as tools in Copilot Studio agents, configure a data policy with the connectors you want to block.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Advanced Connector Policies govern certified connectors and MCP servers through the hosting environment's policy.
claims.quote: ACP offers a modern, flexible approach to managing certified connectors. ... administrators ... can choose to block an entire MCP server. ... At runtime, when a connector operation is invoked, it queries the effective policy for the current hosting environment.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Custom and HTTP connectors are not supported by ACP and still need classic data policies.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported. ... For governing custom connectors and HTTP connectors today, continue using classic data policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: ACP design-time enforcement is rolling out to Copilot Studio; until available there, enforcement is runtime-only.
claims.quote: Design-time enforcement is rolling out across maker portals in the following order: ... Copilot Studio — following Power Automate ... Until design-time support is available in a given maker portal, ACP operates as a runtime-only enforcement for that workload.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Tools, connectors, models and skills blocked by data policies or ACP appear disabled in harness-agent selection lists.
claims.quote: When a data policy or Advanced Connector Policy blocks a tool, connector, AI model, or skill, that item appears disabled wherever you'd normally select it, such as the tools list, model list, or skills list.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy settings are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy when available.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly confirm that the Work IQ MCP tenant policy governs the inline agent node's Work IQ option.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" "Work IQ" "policy". Read node page, Work IQ MCP policy governance and agents-experience/add-work-iq. They describe the node toggle and general Work IQ governance but do not explicitly map that inline-node option to the MCP policy.

claims.claim: Monthly agent limits are documented at Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio > Manage Agents.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center, go to Licensing > Copilot Studio. ... Select Manage Agents. ... Select the agent, and then select Set limit. ... Enter the monthly Copilot Credit limit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP's initial policy control is tenant-level.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, tenant administrators can turn Work IQ MCP policy on or off for the tenant.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests.
claims.quote: It adds a request-time governance layer that can allow or deny specific MCP tool requests based on tenant policy.

claims.claim: Learn does not state that individual-agent monthly limits cap agent-node credit consumption inside a workflow.
claims.quote: Searched: "agent node" monthly limits. Read manage-usage-github-copilot-harness and node page; search returned agent-limit guidance, not a node-specific cap. The separate standard-harness flow guidance does not establish a cap for this workflow node.
